measured_findings: Tail1 reverse slowness reproduced in a fresh process: valid formal 100-pair reverse averages 653.6919 ms per 8 requests; independent 20-pair reverse diagnostic averages 654.3925 ms. All-request lookahead_prepare means are 68.4986/68.6018 ms.

The sole forward tail1 run averages 471.4368 ms per 8 requests and lookahead_prepare 24.8595 ms. Both observed reverse runs are slow; this correlation does not prove execution order causes the slowdown.
Tail0 and tail2 reverse runs remain normal. General reverse-order overhead is therefore not established.

Both slow tail1 runs also slow the lead18 control. Next Encoder device start is delayed about 26 ms after VLM completion, while AE/VLM Event spans remain about 39/42.7 ms. No steady recapture or extra KV slot is recorded; SM allocations and sources match.

The observed excess lies in the preparation/submission critical path, but lookahead_prepare measures wall time containing host transforms, blocking .to(device) and GPU preprocessing. It is not evidence of purely CPU computation slowing down.

The mechanism remains undetermined without synchronized CPU scheduling, prepare substage, and CUDA API evidence for the affected run. Existing profiles are separate runs and cannot establish the anomalous formal/diagnostic cause.

timing_scope.lookahead_prepare_ms: perf_counter around callback prepare(future), after AE Graph submission and before lookahead Vision encode. Includes deepcopy, input transforms, NumPy conversion, Torch .to(device) with default non_blocking=False, and GPU preprocessing; this is host wall time, not pure CPU compute.
timing_scope.next_encoder_start_after_vlm_ms: CUDA Event elapsed_time from current prefix_done to next vision_begin, reported after completion; reflects delayed device start but does not directly timestamp host submission.
timing_scope.cpu_cpu_ms: Prepared input to decoded CPU action including output transform; raw initial preparation is separate.
timing_scope.admission_to_action_ms: Existing misleading name denotes loop-entry to decoded return, not true observation admission.

attribution_bounds.gpu_snapshot_limit: gpu_before is idle and gpu_after contains own process; these endpoint snapshots alone are not continuous interference sampling.
